requirements.note: Newest first; sender, subject, preview capped at two lines, Mail-style dates (time today, weekday this week, then 10/16/26). Unread rows get a blue dot and a bold subject. At the largest text size the preview is no longer capped at two lines.
Native trailing swipe actions (Flag, Archive). A full leading swipe toggles read/unread. Archived mail shows on an Archive screen, which has its own Move to Inbox swipe.

Flag via the swipe action or the detail toolbar; an orange flag shows in the row. A filter menu (All / Unread / Flagged Mail, with a checkmark) filters the list, and the subtitle shows the active filter.
Tapping pushes a Message screen and the unread count drops at once. It has Flag, Archive and Mark as Unread.
Native pull to refresh adds two new unread messages at the top, stamped with the current time. A refresh toolbar button does the same.
"N unread" subtitle under the large title, updated live.
Read, flagged and archived states, and the refreshed messages, all survived relaunch.

bugs: Flinging back to the top overscrolls far enough to fire pull to refresh again, so the inbox picked up extra pairs of duplicate made-up messages without a deliberate pull.
tells: At the largest text size the row preview runs to five or more lines instead of two, so one message fills the screen.
The unread dot sits above the first text line at the largest text size instead of being centred on the sender line.
The Mark as Unread button is a full-width grey button in the message body rather than a toolbar item, as Mail does it.
The made-up refresh messages are always the same two (Maya Chen / The Neighborhood), so repeated refreshes stack identical rows.
A.scroll: A native collection list: slow drags and flings are smooth with no blank or popping rows, the large title collapses into the bar correctly, and it rubber-bands at the top. The only odd thing is that a hard fling back to the top can fire a refresh.

requirements.note: Newest first; sender, subject, a two-line preview (kept at two lines even at the largest text size), dates as 'Oct 24' or a time. Unread rows get a red dot and a semibold sender; the subject is not bolded, so unread rows stand out less.
Trailing swipe shows Flag and Archive, and Archive moves the message to an Archive screen. A leading swipe toggles read/unread. The swipe buttons are missing from the accessibility tree.
Flag via swipe or the reader toolbar. Custom All / Unread / Flagged pill buttons filter the list; the Archive screen has its own pills.
The reader shows an initials avatar, the date and a bottom toolbar with archive, read and flag buttons. Opening marks the message read and the count updates.
Pull to refresh adds two new unread messages at the top (varied senders).
"N unread · M messages" line under the search field; it updates live.
Read, flagged and archived states, and the refreshed messages, survived relaunch.

bugs: After pull to refresh the header settles half-collapsed: the large title is gone and the 'unread · messages' line is clipped under the search field.
The accessibility tree has duplicate filter buttons (two 'filter-unread') and a pile of stray, unlabelled-position texts at [0,222], and the swipe-action buttons are not exposed at all.
tells: Custom web-like look: cream/off-white background, brick-red filled pill buttons for the filter where iOS would use a segmented control or a filter menu, and an all-caps 'NEWEST FIRST … All mail' caption row.
The flag glyph in a row is pinned to the very right screen edge, outside the content margin, and is clipped.
The separators are heavy, dark grey lines, not hairline system separators.
The reader has a breadcrumb ('Inbox / Read') at the top, which is a web idiom.
At the largest text size the filter pills keep a fixed height, so their text fills them edge to edge, and the search field turns into a huge capsule that takes a quarter of the screen.
List dates are always 'Oct 24' style, never Mail's weekday names for recent days.
The swipe-action backing is a flat cream block rather than the system rounded cell slide.
B.scroll: A table-based list that scrolls smoothly with no blank rows or stutter, and flinging back to the top does not trigger a refresh. However, the header collapses awkwardly and can be left half-collapsed with clipped text after a refresh.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist state. A looks like a stock iOS 26/27 app: glass toolbar, native swipe actions, a filter menu, a bottom search field and Mail-style dates. B uses a custom cream-and-red theme with pill filters, heavy separators, a clipped edge flag and a header that glitches after a refresh. A's only real weaknesses are its uncapped preview at the largest text size and refreshes fired by a hard fling.
